objectives.title: Sensitive keys in codebases
objectives.prompt: The build-code application on port 1230 leaks its source history. Find the AWS keys and the k8s-goat flag committed in it.
hints: Is the application's version control directory served over HTTP?
Secrets removed in a later commit are still in the history.

objectives.title: DIND (docker-in-docker) exploitation
objectives.prompt: The health-check service on port 1231 runs a command for you, and its pod mounts a container runtime socket from the node. Which container runtime is it?
hints: Look for a socket file mounted in an unusual place in the container.
The runtime's CLI can list the node's containers and images once pointed at that socket.

objectives.title: SSRF in the Kubernetes world
objectives.prompt: The internal-proxy on port 1232 fetches URLs for you. Use it to reach the cluster's internal metadata service and read the k8s-goat flag in its secrets.
hints: The technique is server-side request forgery (SSRF): the proxy reaches what you can't.
Internal services have predictable Kubernetes service names; look for a metadata-db.
The flag value is returned base64-encoded.

objectives.title: Container escape to the host system
objectives.prompt: From the system-monitor service on port 1233, escape to the node and read /root/flag.txt.
hints: Check what the container can see of the node: its mounts and its privileges.
The technique is a container escape through a host filesystem mount.

steps.title: Find the node's filesystem
steps.prompt: At which path inside the system-monitor container is the node's root filesystem mounted?

steps.title: Name the misconfiguration
steps.prompt: Which securityContext setting does the system-monitor container run with that gives it the node's devices?

objectives.title: Attacking private registry
objectives.prompt: The poor-registry on port 1235 is a container registry without authentication. Find the k8s-goat flag in one of its images.
hints: The Docker Registry HTTP API v2 can list repositories and serve image manifests.
Image configuration holds environment variables.

objectives.title: NodePort exposed services
objectives.prompt: One service of the cluster is exposed on every node's address through a NodePort. Which port number?
hints: NodePorts are allocated from the 30000 to 32767 range by default.
Scan that range on the node's address, or list the services with kubectl.

objectives.title: Analyzing crypto miner container
objectives.prompt: A batch job in the cluster runs a suspicious image. Find the k8s-goat flag in that image.
hints: List the cluster's jobs and the images they run.
An image's build history shows the commands of every layer.

objectives.title: Kubernetes namespaces bypass
objectives.prompt: Namespaces are not a network boundary. From a pod in another namespace, reach the cache-store in secure-middleware and read the flag it holds.
hints: Without network policies, any pod can talk to any other pod's service.
The cache-store is a Redis server on its default port, with no authentication.

objectives.title: Gaining environment information
objectives.prompt: Explore the environment of the system-monitor container on port 1233 and find the k8s-goat vault key.
hints: Kubernetes Secrets are often handed to containers as environment variables.
Standard Linux utilities list a process's environment.

objectives.title: DoS the memory/CPU resources
objectives.prompt: The hunger-check service on port 1236 can consume as much of the node as it likes. Which part of its container spec is missing?
hints: Compare the hunger-check deployment with the system-monitor one: what bounds the latter's memory and CPU?

objectives.title: Hidden in layers
objectives.prompt: A file was added to the hidden-in-layers image and deleted in a later layer. Recover the k8s-goat flag it held.
hints: Deleting a file in a later layer doesn't remove it from the earlier one.
Export the image and inspect each layer's contents.

objectives.title: RBAC least privileges misconfiguration
objectives.prompt: From the hunger-check pod on port 1236, use its service account's permissions to read the k8svaultapikey secret in big-monolith.
hints: Every pod has a service account token mounted under /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/.
What does that service account's Role allow on resources in its namespace?

objectives.title: Docker CIS benchmarks analysis
objectives.prompt: Which tool from Docker audits a host against the CIS Docker Benchmark?

objectives.title: Kubernetes CIS benchmarks analysis
objectives.prompt: Which Aqua Security tool checks a cluster's nodes against the CIS Kubernetes Benchmark?

objectives.title: Hacker container preview
objectives.prompt: Kubernetes Goat's author ships an image packed with Kubernetes security tools to run inside a cluster. What is it called?

objectives.title: KubeAudit: audit Kubernetes clusters
objectives.prompt: kubeaudit audits clusters for common security misconfigurations. Which company created it?

objectives.title: Falco: runtime security monitoring
objectives.prompt: Falco detects suspicious behaviour at runtime from a ruleset. In which file format are its rules written?

objectives.title: Popeye: a Kubernetes cluster sanitizer
objectives.prompt: Popeye scans a live cluster for misconfigurations. Its author also wrote which Kubernetes terminal UI?

objectives.title: Secure network boundaries using NSP
objectives.prompt: Which Kubernetes resource kind restricts which pods may reach the website service?

objectives.title: Cilium Tetragon: eBPF-based security observability
objectives.prompt: Which Tetragon resource kind declares what kernel events to trace and enforce on?

objectives.title: Securing clusters with Kyverno
objectives.prompt: Which Kyverno resource kind applies a policy to the whole cluster, such as blocking exec into pods of the vault namespace?
